sources.entry: Draw.io Drawio is a diagramming and whiteboarding desktop app [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop)

summary.one_liner: drawio-desktop is an Electron-based desktop app that wraps the draw.io diagramming editor for Windows, macOS and Linux.
keywords: make a flowchart on my mac
diagram app that does not send data
summary.what_it_does: The repository packages the draw.io web diagram editor as a desktop application using Electron. The README points to prebuilt binaries on the releases page for Windows (NSIS installer, MSI, portable zip, Microsoft Store APPX, and ARM64 variants), macOS, and Linux (AppImage, deb, rpm, Snap, Flatpak). It describes an update mechanism that checks for new versions in the background on some install types, and store-managed updates for Store, Snap and Flatpak. It states that diagram data is not sent externally and that the web interface's Content Security Policy blocks remotely loaded JavaScript, though diagrams can still trigger fetches of external media they reference. Developers can run it from source with npm, using the draw.io editor as a git submodule. The README says the project is closed to outside contributions.
use_cases: create flowcharts and diagrams offline on desktop
install a portable diagram editor without admin rights
draw whiteboard-style diagrams on macOS or Linux
run a privacy-focused diagram app that keeps data local
deploy a centrally managed diagram app with updates disabled
how_to_run: npm start (in the repo root) to run the app
export DRAWIO_ENV=dev for dev mode (internal use only)
See doc/BUILDING_FOR_PERSONAL_USE.md to build an unsigned app for personal use
notable: Windows installer options: per-machine NSIS, per-user MSI, and a portable zip needing no admin rights
Content Security Policy blocks remotely loaded JavaScript; the README says no diagram data or analytics are sent externally
Update checks can be disabled with DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE or --disable-update
Wraps the existing draw.io web editor rather than a separate codebase
caveats: The README states the project is closed to outside contributions unless a maintainer permits it
Support is only via the repo, with no contractual commitment and no private ticketing for non-paying users
AppImageLauncher 2.2.0 cannot load the static AppImage runtime used since 31.4.2; a 3.x release is needed
The MSI and Microsoft Store builds are x64 only and run under emulation on ARM64 devices
ARM64 builds up to and including 31.4.4 shipped with auto-update disabled
